subject: math

objective.text: Compare numbers by the value of their digits. Order numbers from least to greatest.

explanations.title: Compare the largest unit first
explanations.text: Find the largest unit in both numbers. The number with more of that unit is greater.

explanations.title: If the largest units are equal
explanations.text: If the digits of the largest unit are equal, compare the next place right.

explanations.title: Comparison symbols
explanations.text: Greater than is >. Less than is <. Equal to is =. Say a comparison in two ways.

explanations.title: Order several numbers
explanations.text: Write the numbers in the place value chart. Find the first place where they differ. Then order them.

explanations.title: Numbers in different forms
explanations.text: Write the first number in standard form. Then compare place by place.

examples.title: 3,010 and 2,040
examples.text: Thousands is the largest unit. 3 thousands is greater than 2 thousands, so 3,010 > 2,040.

examples.title: 43,021 and 45,302
examples.text: Both have 4 ten thousands. 3 thousands is less than 5 thousands, so 43,021 < 45,302.

examples.title: Three numbers in order
examples.text: 32,644 > 32,534 > 32,434. All three have 3 ten thousands and 2 thousands. The hundreds differ.

examples.title: 700,000 + 30,000 + 20 + 8 and 735,008
examples.text: The first number is 730,028. 730,028 < 735,008 because 0 thousands is less than 5 thousands.

hints.text: Think of the multiplication fact with the same numbers. Count by fours.
Say the number of tens. Then say it as a number.
Say the digit and its place. Then say its value.
Use each digit once. Look at the biggest and smallest number allowed.
Find the largest unit in each number. Compare the digits of that unit.
If the digits are equal, move one place to the right and compare there.
Compare the digits from the largest unit. Say the greater number first.
Find the greatest or least number first. Then find the next one.
Write both numbers in standard form first. Then compare them.

misconceptions.label: Compares a smaller unit first
misconceptions.description: The child compares a smaller unit, like the tens, when the largest units differ.
detection_signals: says 2,040 is greater than 3,010 because 4 tens is more than 1 ten
misconceptions.response_text: Start with the largest unit. 3 thousands is greater than 2 thousands, so you do not need the tens.

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses disks on a paper chart. The child cannot draw them.
assets_required.description: A place value chart to hundred thousands with two numbers placed one above the other. The child picks greater than, less than or equal to and the chart shows which place decides.
must_show_exactly: Columns in order: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands
Two rows for the two numbers with digits in the columns
A highlight on the first column where the digits differ
Three buttons: greater than, less than, equal to
A text box where the child types or says two numbers
states_or_frames: Two numbers placed in the chart
The comparison sentence shown in two ways
assets_required.interaction: Child enters two numbers and picks the symbol. The chart highlights the first place that differs.
assets_required.alt_text: A place value chart with two numbers stacked and the deciding place highlighted.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean place value chart with six labeled columns, two rows of digits, and one highlighted column. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source charts are blank pictures. Build from the printed headings.
